items.followUp: Differentiate between the moment of a force and a couple.

rubric.why: Identifies torque as the turning effect of a force and its measure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining torque as the turning effect of a force, or giving its measure as force multiplied by perpendicular distance from the axis.

rubric.why: Identifies the characteristic forces that form a couple.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a couple consists of two equal, opposite and parallel forces.

rubric.why: Defines the centre of mass in terms of the body's mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the centre of mass as the point at which the body's mass may be considered concentrated, or an equivalent statement about its mass distribution.

rubric.why: Defines the centre of gravity by reference to the body's weight.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the centre of gravity as the point through which the body's weight acts.

modelAnswer: Torque is the turning effect of a force about an axis; its magnitude is force multiplied by the perpendicular distance from the axis: τ = Fd.
A couple consists of two equal, opposite and parallel forces acting along different lines; it produces rotation.
The centre of mass is the point at which the mass of a body may be considered concentrated.
The centre of gravity is the point through which the weight of a body acts.
In a uniform gravitational field, the centre of mass and centre of gravity coincide.

items.followUp: Define braking and explain why a vehicle may skid.

rubric.why: Explains that braking reduces or stops a vehicle's motion through applying its brakes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that braking is applying brakes to reduce or stop a vehicle's motion.

rubric.why: Identifies skidding as the tyres sliding or slipping on the road when they lose grip.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that skidding occurs when tyres lose grip and slide or slip on the road.

modelAnswer: Braking is the action of applying brakes to reduce or stop the motion of a vehicle.
Skidding occurs when the tyres lose their grip on the road and slide or slip instead of rolling normally.
